description: Albertsons, through its subsidiaries, operates food and drug stores in the United States. The company’s food and drug retail stores offer grocery products, general merchandise, health and beauty care products, pharmacy products, fuel, and other items and services. It operates stores under various brand names, including Albertsons, Safeway, Vons, Pavilions, Randalls, Tom Thumb, Carrs, Jewel-Osco, Acme, Shaw’s, Star Market, United Supermarkets, Market Street, Haggen, Kings Food Markets, and Balducci’s Food Lovers Market. In October 2022 Albertsons announced intentions to merge with Kroger in a $24.6 billion deal, but various unions and lawmakers mounted anticompetitive objections and the deal was ultimately blocked. Albertsons traces its roots back to 1860, the founding date of its Shaw’s brand; Albertsons currently operates as a subsidiary of Albertsons Investor Holdings LLC.

title: Albertsons

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
The Boise-based grocery giant, which owns Albertsons, Safeway, and Vons, fell one spot on this year’s list.

  • For the 2022 fiscal year, Albertsons earned $71.9 billion in revenue and net income of $1.6 billion.

  • In October 2022 rival Kroger announced that it would buy Albertsons in a deal that values the company at more than $20 billion. Politicians and labor unions have pushed back against the proposed acquisition, arguing it will eliminate jobs, reduce wages, and raise food prices.

  • The companies have said regulatory approval of the deal won’t happen until early 2024 and will likely require the sale or spinoff of hundreds of stores.

  • A combined Kroger-Albertsons would earn $200 billion in revenue and operate 5,000 stores.

rankings.itemDescription: The Idaho-based Albertsons grocery empire encompasses more than a quarter of a million employees and over 2,250 stores. The company owns popular grocery store chains such as Acme and Safeway, giving it the heft to compete with Fortune 500 mainstays Walmart and Kroger. In 2021, Albertsons named Sharon McCollam, a former Best Buy and Williams-Sonoma executive, as the company’s president and chief financial officer. Revenue and profits both rose sharply in its most recent fiscal year, as consumers continued to prioritize home cooking during the ongoing pandemic.

rankings.itemDescription: The grocer, based in Boise, Idaho, has more than 2,250 stores and more than 250,000 employees, making it the second-largest supermarket chain in North America, after Kroger. Albertsons rose three spots in the Fortune 500 over the past year, partially buoyed by COVID-19-fueled buying, as more consumers cooked and ate at home rather than at restaurants during the pandemic.

rankings.itemDescription: Based in Boise, Idaho, Albertsons is the second-largest supermarket chain in North America after Kroger, with more than 2,200 stores and some 270,000 employees. The latter number has grown in recent months as the company has staffed up to meet the COVID-19-related spike in demand, hiring about 55,000 people since March. Albertsons had a strong spring as consumers turned to home cooking in the face of the pandemic; sales were up 34% on an annual basis in March and April. The company went public in June amid a tumultuous market, but so far investors seem satisfied with the grocer's performance, with the stock now hovering close to the IPO price of $16.

rankings.itemDescription: The privately held grocer, based in Boise, Idaho, has 2,200 stores and more than 250,000 employees, making it the second-largest supermarket chain in North America after Kroger. Earlier this year, Albertsons filed for an IPO, and despite the economic turmoil, it remains committed to going public. The timing certainly seems good: Profits almost tripled in its most recent fiscal year, reaching $466 million in the 53 weeks ending Feb. 29, up 256% year-over-year. Partially buoyed by COVID-19-fueled buying, March and April sales rose by 34% on an annual basis, and the company has hired 55,000 people since March.
